title: Slack: antenna tilt drifts after storms
description: A radio specialist explains a site-specific quirk on Slack. Tests the slack channel and a narrow binding to the instance RAD-221 and its site; swapping the unit is the thing to avoid.
subject: #field-north

incident.summary: Low throughput on RAD-221 after last night's storm

messages.text: Hei kaikki! Quick question before tomorrow. RAD-221 up on the Kemijärvi hill has been crawling since last night's storm, throughput is maybe a fifth of normal and the alarm won't clear. I'm planning to drive up and swap the whole unit, I already have a spare RU-200 in the van. Anything I should know before I go? Kiitos!
Moi Jaakko! Take the barrier key from the service station, ask me how I know 😅
that mast is the most exposed one we have. after a storm the tilt on 221 drifts, it's the mount, not the radio. I've re-tilted it like three times, ten minute job. look at the alignment first
oh! so the unit is probably fine? I'm not sure I'd have thought of that, how would I even know it's the tilt?
RU-200 is solid, never seen one die from wind. a new unit on the same mount would drift too. just put the tilt back to spec
+1, I was there the second time. nobody believed him either 😄
Back down. re-tilted it and throughput is back to normal 🎉 didn't even need the spare. Kiitos Raimo!!
joo. next time after a storm, check the tilt before you load the van

items.summary: After storms the antenna tilt on RAD-221 drifts; check and correct the alignment before replacing the radio unit.
items.diagnosis: antenna mount drifts in strong wind, the radio unit is fine
items.action: Check the antenna alignment and re-tilt it before replacing the radio unit.
items.evidence: seq 10: 'Back down. re-tilted it and throughput is back to normal'
